rites.name: Moreron
rites.text: Moreron is a concept of Kaktun held in the Courts, an age when divine trials were judged and the doors between worlds were first raised. It is remembered as the idea that a threshold must be weighed before it can be crossed.

rites.name: Drouktak
rites.text: Drouktak is a concept of Kaktun, a notion of an ember-bearing trial-judge who presides over the Courts during the Holy Age of flame and temples. Its role is to weigh oaths sworn before the builders of the doors between worlds, and it is remembered mostly through the sentences it handed down.

rites.name: Thaikuthun
rites.text: Thaikuthun is a concept in the Kaktun universe, an idea of the Courts that names the principle by which doors between worlds are measured and set. It was framed during the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke old bonds and the councils needed a shared term for what held a threshold together.

rites.name: Miilys
rites.text: Miilys is a concept in the Kaktun universe, conceived during the Seeding when makers plant the Weave and quiet powers sleep. It belongs to the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke old bonds between the peoples of the land.

rites.name: Goukozhoth
rites.text: Goukozhoth is a concept in Kaktun's Age of Sundering, a force that the Fall and the Pact both reference while the shards of broken worlds drifted apart. It is remembered as the pressure that made landfall tear old bonds loose across the Grounded Realm.

rites.name: Gakourkurn
rites.text: Gakourkurn is a concept in Kaktun's Walled Age, a principle of holding walls that the orders and churches built their first crossings upon. It is remembered during the Age of the first sovereign, when groves and growing kingdoms took shape around it.

rites.name: Khornaiktar
rites.text: Khornaiktar is a fenwater-born spirit-current that coils through the reeds of Kaktun's grounded marshes, answering to rhythmic song rather than blood or chant. Its pale azure forms begin as humble veils and buzzing motes, but the longer a singer keeps them bound, the more they learn to think and to cling to a body as borrowed limbs and plated armor.

rites.name: Draikun
rites.text: Draikun is a pale, humming resonance that forms when two mismatched wills align in a single shared breath, lending a blended hue to the air around them. Its bearers in the Kaktun grounded realm use it to mend fractured bonds and to stabilize wild emotional storms, though it is fragile and fades if either partner withdraws. It sits quietly in the third age as a tool for reconciliation rather than conquest.

rites.name: Vhuggun
rites.text: Vhuggun is a quiet sensory discipline practiced in the Kaktun grounded realm, where practitioners tint their own irises and the veins beneath their skin through a shifting palette of named hues to signal feeling they cannot speak. The shade rises and falls with anger, sorrow, longing, and gentleness, so a skilled reader can follow an entire argument without a single word being exchanged.
